title: 121. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Converting Metric Volume Units
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a volume given in litres to millilitres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(3\text{ L}\) to \(\text{mL}\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ L}=1{,}000\text{ mL}\), multiply \(3\) by \(1{,}000\): \(3\times 1{,}000=3{,}000\). Therefore, \(3\text{ L}=3{,}000\text{ mL}\). Option A incorrectly uses \(100\text{ mL}\) per litre.
questions.hint: Use the meaning of the prefix milli- to relate the two units.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a volume given in millilitres to litres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(5{,}000\text{ mL}\) to \(\text{L}\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1{,}000\text{ mL}=1\text{ L}\), divide \(5{,}000\) by \(1{,}000\): \(5{,}000\div 1{,}000=5\). Therefore, \(5{,}000\text{ mL}=5\text{ L}\). Option B incorrectly divides by \(100\).
questions.hint: Use the meaning of the prefix milli- and decide whether the target unit is larger or smaller.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a volume given in cubic metres to litres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(2.5\text{ m}^3\) to \(\text{L}\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ m}^3=1{,}000\text{ L}\), multiply \(2.5\) by \(1{,}000\): \(2.5\times 1{,}000=2{,}500\). Therefore, \(2.5\text{ m}^3=2{,}500\text{ L}\). Option A incorrectly multiplies by \(100\).
questions.hint: Choose a unit conversion that cancels the source volume unit.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a volume given in cubic centimetres to litres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(4{,}500\text{ cm}^3\) to \(\text{L}\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ L}=1{,}000\text{ cm}^3\), divide \(4{,}500\) by \(1{,}000\): \(4{,}500\div 1{,}000=4.5\). Therefore, \(4{,}500\text{ cm}^3=4.5\text{ L}\). Option A incorrectly divides by \(100\).
questions.hint: Distinguish a cubic length unit from a litre-based unit.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a volume given in litres to cubic centimetres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(7.2\text{ L}\) to \(\text{cm}^3\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ L}=1{,}000\text{ cm}^3\), multiply \(7.2\) by \(1{,}000\): \(7.2\times 1{,}000=7{,}200\). Therefore, \(7.2\text{ L}=7{,}200\text{ cm}^3\). Option A incorrectly multiplies by \(100\).
questions.hint: A cubic measurement contains three length factors.

questions.concept: Converting Cubic Metres to Cubic Centimetres
questions.learningObjective: Convert a volume given in cubic metres to cubic centimetres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(0.8\text{ m}^3\) to \(\text{cm}^3\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ m}=100\text{ cm}\), cubing gives \(1\text{ m}^3=(100)^3\text{ cm}^3=1{,}000{,}000\text{ cm}^3\). Therefore, \(0.8\text{ m}^3=0.8\times 1{,}000{,}000\text{ cm}^3=800{,}000\text{ cm}^3\). Option B incorrectly uses \(100{,}000\text{ cm}^3\) per cubic metre.
questions.hint: Choose a unit conversion that cancels the source volume unit.

questions.learningObjective: Convert a volume given in millilitres to cubic centimetres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(3{,}600\text{ mL}\) to \(\text{cm}^3\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ mL}=1\text{ cm}^3\), the numerical value stays the same. Therefore, \(3{,}600\text{ mL}=3{,}600\text{ cm}^3\). Option B incorrectly divides by \(10\).
questions.hint: Distinguish a cubic length unit from a litre-based unit.

questions.concept: Converting Cubic Millimetres to Cubic Centimetres
questions.learningObjective: Convert a volume given in cubic millimetres to cubic centimetres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(12{,}000\text{ mm}^3\) to \(\text{cm}^3\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ cm}=10\text{ mm}\), cubing gives \(1\text{ cm}^3=1{,}000\text{ mm}^3\). Therefore, \(12{,}000\text{ mm}^3=12{,}000\div 1{,}000\text{ cm}^3=12\text{ cm}^3\). Option B incorrectly divides by \(100\).
questions.hint: A cubic measurement contains three length factors.

questions.concept: Converting Cubic Metres to Cubic Decimetres
questions.learningObjective: Convert a volume given in cubic metres to cubic decimetres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(0.45\text{ m}^3\) to \(\text{dm}^3\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ m}=10\text{ dm}\), cubing gives \(1\text{ m}^3=1{,}000\text{ dm}^3\). Therefore, \(0.45\text{ m}^3=0.45\times 1{,}000\text{ dm}^3=450\text{ dm}^3\). Option A incorrectly uses \(100\text{ dm}^3\) per cubic metre.
questions.hint: Choose a unit conversion that cancels the source volume unit.

questions.concept: Converting Cubic Centimetres to Cubic Metres
questions.learningObjective: Convert a volume given in cubic centimetres to cubic metres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(250{,}000\text{ cm}^3\) to \(\text{m}^3\).
questions.hint: A cubic measurement contains three length factors.
